pins.name: GPIO0
pins.label: GPIO0 (Button)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. Onboard FLASH/BOOT pushbutton (one of two 'reset/flash buttons' on this board per official esp8266/Arduino core board docs) - see chipGpios note
Onboard FLASH/BOOT button (active-low, standard ESP8266 GPIO0 boot-mode-select convention) - confirmed present via official esp8266/Arduino core board docs ('two reset/flash buttons'); no board-specific schematic found - see notes.txt

pins.name: GPIO1
pins.label: GPIO1
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: GPIO2
pins.label: GPIO2 (Button)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH at boot. Onboard USER button (active-low, INPUT_PULLUP) - confirmed via vendor blog + official ESPert library source, see chipGpios note
Onboard USER button (active-low, INPUT_PULLUP) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: GPIO3
pins.label: GPIO3
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: SS
pins.label: SS (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: GPIO16
pins.label: GPIO16 (Led active low)
pins.notes:
RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Onboard green LED (active-low, LED_BUILTIN) - confirmed via vendor blog + official ESPert library source, see chipGpios note. Using this pin for deep-sleep wake (RST) disables the LED, and vice versa, per vendor docs
Onboard green LED (active-low, LED_BUILTIN) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0, labelled "AD" on this board's silkscreen) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. Vendor docs state a 0-3.3V max input range (on-board divider) rather than the bare chip's native 0-1.0V - see adc note below
